evidence: ADNI recruits participants aged 55-90 years with memory complaints, mild cognitive impairment, or Alzheimer's disease dementia
learning: ADNI stratified sampling: three diagnostic categories (normal, MCI, AD) with unequal allocation (200/400/200)

evidence: ADNI follows participants for 5-10 years with assessments every 6-12 months depending on diagnosis category
learning: ADNI visit frequency varies by diagnosis: annual for stable groups, biannual for MCI converters

evidence: CSF biomarkers measured: Aβ42, Aβ40, total-tau, phosphorylated-tau-181
learning: ADNI biomarker cascade uses both CSF (amyloid/tau) and plasma (NfL/p-tau) for neurodegeneration tracking

evidence: Plasma biomarkers include: plasma Aβ42/40 ratio, p-tau181, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP
learning: ADNI biomarker cascade uses both CSF (amyloid/tau) and plasma (NfL/p-tau) for neurodegeneration tracking

evidence: MRI protocol includes: T1-weighted MP-RAGE, T2-weighted, FLAIR, and functional sequences
learning: ADNI MRI uses standardized 3T protocol with phantom quality control across all acquisition sites

evidence: Primary outcome: Alzheimer's disease dementia diagnosis; Secondary: cognitive decline rate
learning: ADNI defines progression outcome as composite: CDR increase OR clinical dementia diagnosis

evidence: ADNI data organized in tabular CSV files with standardized variable names and visit codes
learning: ADNI data model uses explicit visit codes tied to calendar time points (baseline, 6-month, 12-month, year2-5)

evidence: Data access requires ADNI Data Use Agreement and NIH approval
learning: ADNI data access requires formal governance process (DUA + NIH approval) with exclusion criteria

evidence: Progression criteria: conversion from MCI to AD dementia documented by ADNI criteria
learning: ADNI progression modeling incorporates genetic risk (ApoE) and biomarker thresholds for stratification

evidence: Progression outcome defined as: CDR increase >=1 point or AD dementia diagnosis
